name: The Fall
label: Matador
lede: Forty-two years, thirty-one studio albums, twenty-four Peel sessions and roughly sixty musicians hired and fired by one man from Prestwich, who stayed until the very end.

eras.title: Camus, biscuit tins and the Sex Pistols
eras.text: Four friends from Prestwich and Salford saw the Sex Pistols and decided to make something stranger. Within two years half of them were gone, and Mark E. Smith's way of running a band was already set.

years.h: The Sex Pistols gig that starts The Fall
years.p: Mark E. Smith, [[Martin Bramah|d956f22a-27bf-45a0-9362-821eea53ddbb]], [[Una Baines|8afef734-a652-494e-b25e-0ff895fba38e]] and Tony Friel see the Sex Pistols at Manchester's Lesser Free Trade Hall. Friel names the band after Albert Camus's novel The Fall.
years.xp: Smith was a shipping clerk at the Salford docks at the time, after a first job in a meat factory. The four met to read each other's writing and take drugs. Baines couldn't afford a drum kit, so she played biscuit tins before switching to keyboards.

years.h: First gig: a basement, and a drummer nobody could name
years.p: The Fall's first show is in the North West Arts basement in Manchester. Writer Dave Simpson identified the drummer 34 years later: Steve Ormrod, who lasted one gig over politics.
years.xp: [[Karl Burns|4c79d249-fed7-4d8f-a05a-eeb96a6bdd02]], who had played with Friel in Nuclear Angel, took over on drums. That November, [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]] manager Richard Boon paid for the first recording session.

years.h: Tony Friel quits over Kay Carroll's management
years.p: Kay Carroll, Mark E. Smith's girlfriend, becomes manager. Bassist Tony Friel doesn't like it, leaves, and forms The Passage.

years.h: Una Baines leaves after an overdose and breakdown
years.p: Keyboardist Una Baines leaves The Fall after a drug overdose and a nervous breakdown. Yvonne Pawlett replaces her.

years.h: Bassist quits over a Hawaiian shirt at a Peel session
years.p: Eric McGann walks out of The Fall in disgust because van driver Steve Davies wore a Hawaiian shirt to the band's first [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] session. There would be 24 Peel sessions in all.

years.h: Bingo-Master's Break-Out! EP · Step Forward
years.p: The Fall's first record, from the session Richard Boon paid for the previous November.

eras.title: Hip priests and two drummers
eras.text: A 16-year-old roadie became the bassist, two lads from a support band became the backbone for nearly two decades, and The Fall made the records Peel played for the rest of his life. Then Smith sacked the one member who fought back.

years.h: Roadie Marc Riley, 16, is promoted to bass
years.p: Marc Riley goes from carrying The Fall's gear to playing in the band. He moves to guitar in April.

years.h: Live at the Witch Trials, recorded in one day
years.p: The Fall's debut album was cut in a single day in December 1978. Soon after, Martin Bramah leaves to form [[Blue Orchids|62c562c9-f91d-4195-8924-86be20ab9d41]] with Una Baines, and Karl Burns quits.

years.h: Craig Scanlon and Steve Hanley join from Staff 9
years.p: The Fall takes guitarist Craig Scanlon and bassist Steve Hanley from support band Staff 9. Hanley's bass would define the sound for 19 years.

years.h: Dragnet: the studio complains about the sound
years.p: Cargo Studios in Rochdale protested the murky sound of Dragnet, worried it would put off other bands.

years.h: Paul Hanley, 16 and still at school, joins on drums
years.p: Drummer Mike Leigh quit for the cabaret circuit after weeks without work. Steve Hanley's younger brother Paul debuts at London's Electric Ballroom.

years.h: Grotesque tops the UK indie chart
years.p: The Fall's first album for Rough Trade after the live-and-rehearsal set Totale's Turns, where Mark E. Smith can be heard ordering drinks and berating the band.

q: a bunch of well-meaning but inept hippies
years.h: The Fall walks out on Rough Trade
years.p: Mark E. Smith leaves Rough Trade over politics and signs with Kamera. Paul Hanley is too young for a US visa, so Karl Burns returns for the tour and stays as a second drummer.

years.h: Hex Enduction Hour, partly recorded in a lava-walled studio
years.p: Two drummers, sessions in Reykjavík's Hljóðriti and a disused cinema in Hitchin. HMV racked the crude cover backwards.
years.xp: It sold 20,000 copies by mid-1983. Its lyrics reportedly cost The Fall a Motown deal in 1984, and a piece of Hip Priest turns up in The Silence of the Lambs.

years.h: Marc Riley is sacked after a fistfight in Australia
years.p: After rows including a fistfight on the Australian tour, Mark E. Smith fires Marc Riley. Riley's new band The Creepers answers with Jumper Clown, mocking Smith's clothes.

eras.title: Brix
eras.text: A guitarist from California married Smith within three months of meeting him and pulled The Fall toward hooks. It was their most popular run, with covers in the UK charts and a ballet, and it ended with a divorce.

years.h: Brix Smith marries Mark E. Smith and joins The Fall
years.p: Brix Smith met Mark E. Smith at Chicago's Metro on April 23 and married him on July 19. Her first Fall gig is September 21 at the Hellfire Club, Wakefield.

years.h: Perverted by Language, Brix's first Fall album
years.p: The Fall's last album for Rough Trade, back for one record. A live album from New Zealand, In a Hole, comes out on Flying Nun the same month.

years.h: The Hanley brothers quit after a gear theft
years.p: Steve and Paul Hanley both leave after The Fall's equipment is stolen. Steve Hanley returns midway through the next album.

years.h: This Nation's Saving Grace · Beggars Banquet
years.p: John Leckie produces; Brix Smith and Craig Scanlon write most of the riffs. [[LCD Soundsystem|2aaf7396-6ab8-40f3-9776-a41c42c8e26b]]'s James Murphy later called it formative.
years.xp: Simon Wolstencroft takes over as sole drummer afterwards, staying about 11 years.

years.h: The Fall hits No. 30 with There's a Ghost in My House
years.p: A cover of R. Dean Taylor's Motown song becomes The Fall's biggest hit so far. Victoria, a [[The Kinks|17b53d9f-5c63-4a09-a593-dde4608e0db9]] cover, reaches No. 35 in 1988.

years.h: I Am Kurious Oranj, a ballet with Michael Clark
years.p: The Fall makes I Am Kurious Oranj as the music for a ballet project with dancer Michael Clark.

years.h: Brix Smith leaves The Fall and divorces Mark E. Smith
years.p: The marriage and Brix Smith's first run in the band end together. Founding guitarist Martin Bramah returns for the next album, Extricate.

eras.title: Top ten, on Matador in America
eras.text: The Fall spent three albums on a major, then went back to indie labels in the UK while Matador Records put them out in the US. They scored their highest chart placing, got Brix back, and lost Scanlon.

years.h: The Infotainment Scan enters the UK chart at No. 9
years.p: The Fall's highest-charting album, out on Permanent in the UK and Matador in the US, includes a [[Sister Sledge|1ed00158-c6a3-45cd-819c-2f91997fc480]] cover. NME said it stood at the peak of their canon.

years.h: Middle Class Revolt, with Karl Burns back
years.p: Karl Burns drums on a Fall album for the first time since 1985. Covers include The Monks' Shut Up!, and Hey! Student places second in Peel's Festive Fifty.

years.h: Julia Nagle joins, and Brix Smith returns
years.p: Julia Nagle comes in on keyboards, guitar and computers. Ex-wife Brix Smith rejoins for Cerebral Caustic and The Light User Syndrome, then leaves again in 1996.

years.h: Craig Scanlon is sacked after 16 years
years.p: Mark E. Smith fires guitarist Craig Scanlon when keyboardist Dave Bush joins [[Elastica|46693641-1e2e-4aae-80ed-6b28170de63a]]. Smith later said he regretted it.

years.h: Levitate flirts with drum and bass
years.p: Simon Wolstencroft quits mid-recording and Karl Burns replaces him again. NME's Steven Wells gives it a rave.

eras.title: Brownies, and after
eras.text: A New York show in 1998 ended with Smith arrested and the rhythm section gone for good. He rebuilt with whoever would stay, and by 2008 found a line-up that lasted to the end.

years.big: One gig, one arrest, three exits
years.h: The Fall falls apart at Brownies in New York
years.p: On the last night of a short US tour, Mark E. Smith unplugs amps mid-song and Karl Burns shoves him. The next day Smith is arrested for assaulting Julia Nagle at the hotel.
years.xp:
Smith said it was a heated argument about sharing a room. According to Wikipedia he was ordered into alcohol and anger-management treatment, and the charges were later dropped. Nagle stayed in the band.

Steve Hanley, after 19 years, left with Karl Burns and guitarist Tommy Crooks. Hanley told the story in his 2014 memoir The Big Midweek.

years.h: The Marshall Suite, Smith and Nagle as a duo
years.p: Mark E. Smith and Julia Nagle rebuild The Fall with hired players for this and The Unutterable (2000).

years.h: Elena Poulou, Mark E. Smith's third wife, joins
years.p: Elena Poulou joins on keyboards. Q names The Fall among its 50 Bands to See Before You Die.

years.h: BBC Four airs The Wonderful and Frightening World of Mark E Smith
years.p: A full documentary on Mark E. Smith and The Fall. He also reads the classified football results on BBC's Final Score.

years.h: Three members quit four dates into a US tour
years.p: The Fall's guitarist, bassist and drummer walk out four shows in. Mark E. Smith calls it the best thing that ever happened to the band.

years.h: The last Fall line-up locks in
years.p: Pete Greenway, David Spurr and Keiron Melling play on Imperial Wax Solvent and stay to the end. Smith publishes his memoir, Renegade.

eras.title: The only constant
eras.text: The Fall ended its run on Domino and smaller labels with an album almost every year. Former members formed their own band; Smith kept going until he couldn't stand.

years.h: Jeff Mangum picks The Fall for All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: [[Neutral Milk Hotel|a506f761-2c22-4b2f-8a94-bd748c2c8f75]]'s Jeff Mangum chooses The Fall for the ATP festival he curates at Minehead.

years.h: Brix Smith and the Hanleys form Brix & the Extricated
years.p: Brix Smith Start, Steve Hanley and Paul Hanley start their own band out of Fall veterans. Hanley's memoir The Big Midweek comes out the same year.

years.h: Elena Poulou leaves The Fall and the marriage
years.p: Mark E. Smith tells Mojo that Elena Poulou has resigned after Sub-Lingual Tablet. They divorce the same year.

years.h: New Facts Emerge, the 31st and last album
years.p: The Fall's final studio album, made as a four-piece.

years.h: The Fall's last show: Queen Margaret Union, Glasgow
years.p: Mark E. Smith's final performance. On November 29 in Bristol he is too ill to leave the hotel, and the band comes out to apologize.

eras.title: No Fall without Smith
eras.text: Smith's death ended The Fall on the spot; there was never a question of carrying on. What's left is the catalog, now owned by one label, and his leftover vocals.

q: They are always different; they are always the same.
years.h: Mark E. Smith dies at home in Prestwich, aged 60
years.p: Mark E. Smith died of lung and kidney cancer after a long illness. He had been the only constant member through about 60 musicians and 31 albums.
years.xp: According to Wikipedia, falls in his later years had left him with bone fragmentation. His partner and manager at his death was Pamela Vander.

years.h: Cherry Red buys the rights to 40 Fall albums
years.p: Cherry Red Records announces a reissue series and box set.

years.h: Post Script: unused Smith vocals, new music
years.p: Billed as a final album, Post Script sets unused Mark E. Smith vocals to new backing by Simon 'Ding' Archer and Ed Blaney, who call it unheard recordings, not a Fall studio album.
